$comment: One row per supported harness, derived from docs/harness-capability-matrix.md.
This exists so that SETUP.md, prism-doctor and the shipped promise text
cannot disagree about what a harness can do. The matrix is the evidence;
this is the machine-readable consequence of it. Change the matrix and this
changes with it -- never the other way round.
'tier' rests on an EXECUTED PROBE, never on vendor documentation. Tier 1
means a hook registered from repo-local config was observed to fire. Tier 2
means it could not be made to fire, whatever the docs say.
A Tier 2 harness still ships its registration file, marked inert, so the
wiring is in place if the mechanism starts working. What it must NEVER do
is report as enforcing: 'gate_active' is false for those rows, and the
doctor reads this field rather than deciding for itself.

'cli' is the executable name to look for on PATH -- the only way to answer 'which agents does this machine have' without asking. 'wrapper_source' and 'wrapper_dest' are the setup wrapper: where it ships and where that harness looks for it. They live here so bootstrap.sh, prism-doctor and SETUP.md read one list instead of three copies of it.

`command_dest` is where the prism-burndown workflow lands. It is a user-invocable prompt, the same category as the setup wrapper, so it reuses the directory `wrapper_dest` already proved for that harness -- it claims no capability this manifest does not record. `review_dest` is a different thing: that is where the SIX REVIEWER AGENTS go, and it is correctly null for four harnesses because four of them cannot dispatch subagents. The burn-down needs no subagents, so it ships everywhere.

Every `wrapper_dest` and `command_dest` is REPO-LOCAL. Antigravity used to be the exception, writing to ~/.gemini/skills/<name>/SKILL.md on the belief that agy reads nothing from a repository directory. That belief came from one failed attempt which shipped the wrapper as a FLAT file, .agents/skills/prism-setup.md -- but a skill is a DIRECTORY named for the skill containing SKILL.md, so the shape was wrong rather than the location. Measured on agy 1.1.27: a probe at .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md is listed by agy and executed, while ~/.gemini/skills/ -- where PRISM had been installing -- appears nowhere in agy's own skill listing, which names ~/.gemini/config/skills/ instead. The wrapper was being written where the agent could never find it. bootstrap.sh still expands a leading `~/` and announces writing outside the repository, so that promise stays visible if a row ever needs it again; no row needs it now.

`invoke` IS THE LAST LINE OF THE INSTALL AND IT IS NOT UNIFORM. A TEMPLATE, not a value: `{name}` is the user-invocable command being reached, so one field serves prism-setup and prism-burndown alike. It resolves to a slash command on three harnesses, `$name` on Codex, and on Copilot an instruction naming the skill, because Copilot has no per-skill command and picks a skill from its description. Until 0.6.0 every document printed `/prism-setup` and `/prism-burndown` for all five, which is wrong for at least Codex -- so the hand-off dead-ended on its final instruction, on the harnesses nobody had walked by hand. `invoke_probed` records how each value is known, and 'REPORTED' means exactly that: believed, not yet machine-probed.

`launch` is the argv that opens an INTERACTIVE session with that text as its first prompt, `{invoke}` substituted. Read from each CLI's own --help rather than assumed, and it splits two ways: claude, cursor-agent and codex take the prompt positionally, while copilot and agy need `-i`. bootstrap.sh execs it, so the agent replaces the shell and inherits the terminal directly instead of running behind a wrapper process.

claude-code.promise: PRISM checks each file as you write it, verifies the work before Claude Code finishes its turn, and blocks at git push.
claude-code.launch_probed: measured 2026-09-10 on this machine: `claude --help` gives `Usage: claude [options] [command] [prompt]`, documents `prompt  Your prompt` as a positional argument, and says it "starts an interactive session by default, use -p/--print for non-interactive output". So the bare positional IS the interactive-with-prompt form; -p would be the wrong one.

cursor.promise: PRISM checks each file as you write it, blocks at git push, and re-prompts Cursor at turn end rather than blocking it.
cursor.invoke_probed: measured 2026-09-10: wrapper_dest is a .cursor/commands/ file, and Cursor commands are slash commands.
cursor.launch_probed: measured 2026-09-10 on this machine: `cursor-agent --help` gives `Usage: agent [options] [command] [prompt...]` with `prompt  Initial prompt for the agent`, and -p/--print is documented as the separate non-interactive mode.

codex.version_tested: codex-cli 0.151.0; hooks per learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks accessed 2026-08-27; .agents/skills loading verified by probe 2026-09-05
codex.promise: PRISM checks each file as you write it, verifies the work before Codex finishes its turn, and blocks at git push -- once you have trusted the project's hook configuration.
codex.invoke_probed: MEASURED 2026-09-10 against Codex's own bundled skill `openai-docs` (~/.codex/skills/.system/openai-docs). `codex exec --json` with the prompt `$openai-docs` injects the skill body: a control run of the identical prompt WITHOUT the token reported 13951 input tokens and answered LITERAL, while the run with it reported 15109 and answered LOADED:openai-docs -- a 1158-token delta against a 5446-byte SKILL.md, i.e. 4.7 bytes per token, which is what English prose tokenizes at. Asked to quote the file's `Only exception:` sentence it reproduced it VERBATIM with ZERO tool or exec events in the stream, so the text was in context rather than read from disk. Note the probe was `codex exec` (print mode); the interactive form `codex "$name"` that `launch` uses was not separately probed, and `codex --help` still exposes no skills surface to read this off.
codex.launch_probed: measured 2026-09-10 on this machine: `codex --help` gives `Usage: codex [OPTIONS] [PROMPT]` and states "If no subcommand is specified, options will be forwarded to the interactive CLI" -- `exec` is the non-interactive subcommand and is NOT used here. This closes the gap left by `invoke_probed`, which was measured through `codex exec` (print mode) and therefore said nothing about the interactive form this row launches.

copilot.version_tested: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.82; .agents/skills invoked as skill(prism-marker) by probe 2026-09-05, while .github/prompts was not recognised
copilot.inert_reason: Repo-local hook config is ignored on CLI 1.0.81; and Copilot hooks are always fail-open on timeout, every event included.
copilot.re_test_trigger: A Copilot CLI release after 1.0.81 whose notes mention repository-local hook discovery, or a Cloud Agent run observed loading this file.
copilot.invoke_probed: measured 2026-09-10: `copilot help commands` lists every interactive slash command (/init /agent /skills /mcp ...) and NO per-skill one. Copilot selects a skill from its description, so the invocation is an INSTRUCTION naming the skill rather than a prefix. `copilot skill list` confirms .agents/skills/ is read, so the destination is right.
copilot.launch_probed: measured 2026-09-10 on this machine: `copilot --help` documents `-i, --interactive <prompt>  Start interactive mode and automatically execute this prompt`. -p/--prompt is the non-interactive one, so -i is the correct flag and it TAKES the prompt as its value -- which is why the sentence must stay one argument.

antigravity.version_tested: Antigravity CLI 1.1.27; .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md listed and executed by probe 2026-09-05
antigravity.inert_reason: Hooks did not fire in any of six probed configurations, across both modes; the 30s default timeout has no documented maximum, and no subagent boundary event exists.
antigravity.re_test_trigger: Antigravity CLI newer than 1.1.22, or product docs stating a hook timeout maximum.
antigravity.invoke_probed: measured 2026-09-10: `agy --help` documents "slash command and skill expansion".
antigravity.launch_probed: measured 2026-09-10 on this machine: `agy --help` documents `-i  Short alias for --prompt-interactive` and `--prompt-interactive  Run an initial prompt interactively and continue the session`; --print/--prompt is the non-interactive pair.
